title: Hard-coded wall-clock performance thresholds make this test suite flaky
reasoning: The tests assert absolute elapsed-time limits and speedup ratios using very small sample sizes. In Docker, CI, or loaded developer machines, scheduler pauses, cold database/cache state, or slower storage can easily push these timings over fixed limits even when the cache behavior is correct. This creates release/build failures unrelated to functional regressions.
recommendation: Keep correctness assertions in the normal suite and move timing checks behind an opt-in benchmark/performance job, or use pytest-benchmark with calibrated baselines and tolerances. If these tests must remain, avoid strict sub-second thresholds in default test runs.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: These are the tests themselves; they encode the flaky timing behavior rather than guarding against it.
minimumFixScope: Update tests/performance/test_bookmark_cache.py to remove or isolate strict wall-clock assertions from default CI execution.
